# Exact geometry, files in and out

The engine evaluates every program twice over: as meshes for the view and checks, and exactly (OpenCascade B-rep) for STEP. Boxes, cylinders, cones, spheres, profiles (polygons, circles, offsets), extrude, revolve, sweeps, helices, lofts, offsets, booleans, mirrors, fillets, chamfers, pushes, shells and drafts are exact; geometry a program computes as triangles (`fromMesh`) or hulls is exported faceted. Prefer the exact vocabulary when a part will be machined.

- Printing: `/export/<id>.3mf` is the whole shape as one object (separate bodies stay separate shells, so print-in-place mechanisms print whole); the person's Send to Bambu Studio button saves it in ~/Downloads/Iṣẹ́ Studio prints and opens it in Bambu Studio. For print-in-place designs keep ≥ 0.3 mm between moving surfaces, and stand every moving part on the bed where you can: a face printed over a layer gap makes Bambu Studio warn of a "floating cantilever" (herringbone teeth or 45° cones hold parts together instead of a floor; see examples/gearbox-print).
- Out (`./ise export`, or the person's download): STEP and IGES exact (every part named, placed, coloured: what the program painted, else its material's look; painted faces keep their names); `.stpz` (compressed STEP) and `.brep` (OpenCascade BREP) the same shapes; STL, OBJ, PLY and GLB meshes (OBJ and GLB keep an object/node per part; OBJ, PLY and GLB carry colour; GLB is metres, Y up, for viewers and the web, the rest millimetres, Z up); 3MF for printing; DXF for a sheet part; the fabrication zip. `--part <name>` is one part at the origin; fabrication packages include a STEP per distinct part.
- In (`./ise import <file>`, or the person drops it on the view): STEP (also compressed `.stpz`, and `.brep`, stored as STEP) and IGES become a shape `return importStep("<sha>")` / `importIges("<sha>")` of the file's exact bodies (IGES surfaces that close are sewn into solids); STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF/GLB and 3MF become `return importMesh("<sha>")`: triangles, faceted in exact exports, so no fillets or edge picks on them. Bodies are parts named as in the file. Colours the file gives are listed in the program's comment and the import's reply: give the parts real materials from them (a colour says nothing of density). Use `importStep/importIges/importMesh(sha, { material, process })` in your own programs: place, subtract, link parameters around them. A mesh with holes is refused unless repaired: `importMesh(sha, { repair: true })` (see Scans below).
- 2D: DXF and SVG become a sketch on XY named after the file (lines, arcs and circles stay so; splines, ellipses and SVG curves become Béziers; blocks placed; units honoured; moved to start at the origin), unconstrained, ready for `sketch("Name").extrude(3)` or to dimension and edit. DWG cannot be read (its only open reader is GPL): ask for a DXF.
